name: Brain & sleep clock

overlay.caption: light into the eyes tells the brain it is still daytime

does: Shows the brain's night-time sleep signal dropping when bright light reaches the eyes late
Shows falling asleep taking longer as a result
Shows the effect piling up over several nights
doesnt: Measure any real person — the numbers are illustrative teaching values
Include caffeine, noise, stress, naps or what time school starts
Diagnose anything; everyone has nights like this
limits.text: This is a simplified learning model. Real people vary with age, fitness and health. The numbers are illustrative, not measurements of any real person.
limits.wellbeing: If you often can't sleep or feel exhausted every day, that's worth talking about with an adult you trust.

sources: NIH News in Health: 'Tired? Blame your body clock'
